issues.legal_issue: A prior order permitting a party to pursue an appropriate remedy for compensation does not prevent the opposing party from raising a defence that the claim is barred by constructive res judicata.
material_facts: After the earlier execution proceedings, the Supreme Court stated that the claimants were free to pursue an appropriate remedy for compensation for improvements in accordance with law.
The earlier High Court had not decided whether the claimants could raise that compensation claim.
The claimants later sought compensation, and the opposing parties raised constructive res judicata as a defence.
issues.conclusion: The earlier order left the opposing parties free to raise constructive res judicata and other appropriate defences to the later compensation claim.
issues.legal_principle: Permission to pursue an appropriate remedy in accordance with law preserves the opposing party's defences; it does not decide the claim's merits or immunize the claim from Section 11, Explanation IV of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

predicates.later_compensation_proceeding: A claimant brings a later proceeding seeking compensation for improvements.
predicates.earlier_order_allows_remedy_in_accordanc: An earlier court order permits the claimant to pursue an appropriate remedy in accordance with law.
predicates.earlier_order_does_not_decide_the_claim: The earlier order does not decide the compensation claim or bar the opposing party from defending against it.

issues.definition: When a claimant brings a later compensation proceeding under an order that permits an appropriate remedy without deciding the claim, the opposing party may raise available defences.

issues.legal_issue: A stranger to a decree who resists delivery of property may have an independent claim adjudicated in execution proceedings before being dispossessed.
material_facts: The claimants were not parties to the decree for possession.
They obstructed delivery of the property and applied in the execution proceedings before being dispossessed.
They sought to establish an independent right to remain in possession.
issues.conclusion: The claimants could have their independent claim adjudicated in the execution proceedings before dispossession; the remedy was not limited to an application after dispossession.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rules 97, 101 and 103 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 provide for adjudication of resistance to possession, including an independent claim by a stranger to the decree, and treat the resulting order as a decree. Brahmdeo Chaudhary v Rishikesh Prasad Jaiswal, Shreenath v Rajesh and Har Vilas v Mahendra Nath establish that a stranger may seek adjudication before actual delivery of possession and is not confined to the post-dispossession remedy.

predicates.execution_obstruction_proceeding: A decree holder seeks delivery of immovable property through execution proceedings.
predicates.claimant_is_stranger_to_decree: The person asserting a right to the property was not a party to the decree.
predicates.claimant_resists_delivery_before_disposs: The person objects to delivery of the property before being dispossessed.

issues.definition: In an execution proceeding, a stranger to the decree who resists delivery before dispossession may have an independent property claim adjudicated at that stage.

issues.legal_issue: A later claim for compensation that could and ought to have been raised in an earlier execution proceeding is barred by constructive res judicata when it is closely connected to the earlier claim to resist possession.
material_facts: In the earlier execution application, the claimants sought a declaration that they were entitled to remain in possession as lessees and that the decree holders could not dispossess them.
The earlier application did not assert a claim for compensation for improvements under the applicable improvements legislation.
The claimants later sought to remain in possession until compensation for improvements was determined and paid.
The compensation claim was connected to the earlier attempt to resist delivery of possession, and the execution proceedings provided a means to have the claim adjudicated.
issues.conclusion: The later compensation claim was barred by constructive res judicata because it could and ought to have been raised in the earlier execution proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11, Explanation IV of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 deems a matter directly and substantially in issue if it might and ought to have been raised in the earlier proceeding; the requirements are conjunctive. Whether a matter ought to have been raised depends on the scope of the earlier proceeding and the matter's connection to the controversy. The principle serves finality and prevents multiplicity of proceedings, as explained in Kameswar Pershad v Rajkumari Ruttun Koer, Henderson v Henderson, Greenhalgh v Mallard, Johnson v Gore Wood & Co, State of U.P. v Nawab Hussain, Direct Recruit Class II Engineering Officers' Association v State of Maharashtra and Forward Construction Co. v Prabhat Mandal. Order XXI Rules 97 to 103 provide a complete execution remedy for claims relating to possession. Sections 4 and 5 of the Kerala Compensation for Tenants Improvements Act, 1958 provide for compensation and continued possession pending eviction, and support raising such a claim in the proceeding determining the right to possession.

rule.if: execution_obstruction_proceeding and earlier_possession_claim_adjudicated and later_claim_seeks_possession_pending_compensation and compensation_claim_could_have_been_raised_earlier and compensation_claim_ought_to_have_been_raised_earlier

predicates.execution_obstruction_proceeding: A claimant resists delivery of property in a proceeding to execute a decree for possession.
predicates.earlier_possession_claim_adjudicated: The claimant's earlier request to remain in possession was adjudicated in the execution proceeding.
predicates.later_claim_seeks_possession_pending_com: The claimant later seeks to retain possession until compensation for improvements is determined or paid.
predicates.compensation_claim_could_have_been_raise: The claimant had an opportunity to assert the compensation ground in the earlier proceeding.
predicates.compensation_claim_ought_to_have_been_ra: The compensation ground was sufficiently connected to the earlier dispute about possession that it should have been raised there.

issues.definition: When an adjudicated execution claim to remain in possession is followed by a connected compensation-based claim to retain possession, and that compensation ground could and should have been raised earlier, the later claim is barred by constructive res judicata.
